name: AM312 mini PIR motion sensor
description: Tiny digital passive-infrared motion sensor: the Nanyang Senba AM312 has its amplifier, filters and decision logic inside the can, so OUT goes high (about 3 V) for about 2.3 s whenever a warm body moves within about 3-5 m, re-triggering while motion continues. Sensitivity and timing are fixed. Draws only about 15 uA. The module's 3 V LDO lets it run from 2.7-12 V. Sold as: AM312 mini PIR motion sensor module (common 10 mm green board with white dome lens, 3 pins: VCC, OUT, GND).
eli5: A tiny heat-motion detector: when a person or animal walks past, it sets its output pin high for a couple of seconds.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Motion output: about 3 V for ~2.3 s per trigger, 0 V otherwise. Push-pull, safe for 3.3 V GPIOs (middle pin 2).

supplierQuery: AM312 mini PIR motion sensor module
buildNotes: Header order: VCC, OUT, GND. OUT is always the middle pin; the + and - marks are tiny or missing, so check polarity before powering.
VCC can come from 3V3 or 5V: the board's 3 V regulator keeps OUT at about 3 V, so it connects straight to a GPIO.
OUT is active high: 1 for about 2.3 s after motion, then a 2.3 s blockade in which it ignores motion. Timing and sensitivity cannot be adjusted.
Give it up to a minute after power-up to settle before trusting the output.
Point the dome where people move across its view; it senses moving warm bodies, not still ones, and cannot see through glass.

driver.code:
# AM312 mini PIR motion sensor module, MicroPython driver.
# The Nanyang Senba AM312 is a digital PIR detector with its signal processing built in.
# Its REL output is a push-pull logic output (VOH > VDD - 1 V, VOL < 1 V at 10 mA):
#   HIGH (about 3 V) for ~2.3 s after motion is detected, re-triggering while motion continues
#   LOW  (0 V) otherwise; after going low it ignores motion for a ~2.3 s blockade time.
# The common mini module has a 3 V LDO, so OUT is about 3 V even when VCC is 5-12 V and
# connects straight to a 3.3 V GPIO. No pull-up/down is needed.
# Allow about a minute after power-up for the sensor to settle (datasheet steadying time).
from machine import Pin


class AM312:
    def __init__(self, out_pin):
        self.pin = Pin(out_pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(out_pin, int) else out_pin

    def motion(self):
        """True while the sensor reports motion (OUT high)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def on_change(self, handler):
        """Call handler(motion: bool) on every edge of OUT. Pass None to stop."""
        if handler is None:
            self.pin.irq(handler=None)
            return
        self.pin.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING | Pin.IRQ_FALLING,
                     handler=lambda p: handler(p.value() == 1))

example.code:
from am312 import AM312
import time

pir = AM312({OUT})
while True:
    print('MOTION=%d' % pir.motion())
    time.sleep(0.5)
